ModMetaData.name: Regions and Societies
ModMetaData.author: Regions and Societies Team
ModMetaData.description:
Discord Community: https://discord.gg/eVBebZ2N9s Version: v0.2.1 (Target: RimWorld 1.5 / 1.6)
Regions and Societies Official Wiki and Documentation: https://github.com/Regions-and-societies/Core-MMF/wiki
Regions and Societies overhauls the world map into living geography: dynamic geographic provinces with terrain-aware borders, four-tier faction territory ownership, geography-driven faction placement, full regional demographics across seven axes with their own map overlays, a population-density heatmap, trade roads and procedural ruins - all built on the Map Mode Framework. It is the continuation of Regions and Territories under a new identity.
Features: - Geographic Domain Mapping: splits the world into dynamic provinces with clear, terrain-aware boundaries. - Territorial Ownership: a four-tier ladder from exclusive hold to loose claim, shaded on the map, with coastlines and mountains reading as real borders. - Geography-Driven Faction Placement: nations settle as contiguous territory, one settlement per region, weighing established claim against resources, shying away from rivals' ground, and squaring their domains off rather than spidering. - Regional Demographics: every region carries a deterministic demographic profile - age structure, sex ratio, xenotypes, ideoligions, wealth, education and employment - derived from the factions pressing on it, their tech and beliefs, and the land itself. Nothing is stored in your save. - Demographic Map Overlays: seven world-map overlays, one per axis, plus faction territory and population density. - Region Panel Breakdown: the expanded region readout shows the full demographic profile alongside ownership and economics. - Hooks for Other Mods: a public API lets war and drafting mods skew a region's sex ratio (drafts, combat losses) with generational recovery, and lets expansion mods rank territory the way core does. - Procedural Trade Infrastructure: trade roads between settlements and historical ruins across the world map.
*** BEST ON A NEW COLONY - EXISTING SAVES ARE SUPPORTED IN COMPATIBILITY MODE *** A world generated with the mod installed gets everything, including placement rules. A world already in progress is adopted in Compatibility Mode: provinces are drawn and territory is owned and shown, but placement stays with vanilla or whichever mod owns it. The mode is decided once per save and shown under Strict territorial ownership in the mod settings. Removing the mod from an in-progress save is not supported and will log errors.
Requires: Map Mode Framework, Harmony
--- Changelog (v0.2.1) - Hotfix --- - Fixed: the in-game debug actions menu (dev mode) failed to open while the mod was installed. A debug action carried a parameter, which RimWorld cannot bind, so building the menu threw and it never opened. Removed the offending action; the menu now opens normally. No gameplay or save changes.
--- Changelog (v0.2.0) - Regional Demographics --- - Seven demographic axes per region, each with a map overlay, region-panel breakdown and public endpoint: age structure (tech-level pyramids, natalist memes, longevity genes), sex ratio, xenotype castes, ideoligion shares with neighbour belief-similarity, wealth/SES tiers (terrain richness and trade roads count), education tiers, and an occupation mix with employment rate. - Everything is derived on read from the world seed - deterministic on every machine, nothing added to the save file. - Honest DLC degradation: without Biotech the xenotype overlay says "all Baseliner"; without Ideology every region is secular - no flat map pretending to be data. - DemographicHooks API: companion mods can report drafts in progress (transient sex-ratio skew) or combat losses (a generational scar recovering over a configurable number of years, default 15, slider provided). - Territory compactness: faction domains square off instead of spidering, tunable with a new slider; expansion mods can rank candidate provinces with the same public metric. - Dwellings readout: the population tooltip answers for every habitable tile (zero included) as a compass block of the tile and its neighbours.
